# feat: scoped usage and Node-control profile publications

This is a new candidate payload delivery for families 9 and 10. NSD/ns review,
producer-owned vectors and producer adoption remain outstanding. Fixture authority
is labelled candidate input and establishes no external interoperability.

## Exact payload contracts

UsageProfilePublication is `[1, reporter, profiles]`. Reporter is the existing
validated full 32-byte IdentityKey. Profiles is a nonempty array of at most two
existing UsageProfile text identifiers, strictly increasing by UTF-8 bytes:
`l8-completed-io-v1`, `l8-relay-data-v1`. Each identifier references its entire
existing quantity, operation, direction and parameter definition in
[the usage contract](usage-contract-candidate.md). No units, batching policies,
incarnations, sequence domains, custody or historical ownership change.

NodeControlProfilePublication is `[1, membership_scope, 2, capabilities]`.
MembershipScope is exactly `[nsd_id_bstr16, network_id_bstr16]`, reusing the
control exchange encoding and validation (fixed widths, no additional nonzero
predicate). Vocabulary 2 names the existing Node-control protocol. Capabilities
is a nonempty, strictly increasing array of at most five existing unsigned kind
numbers: ACK 0, ENDPOINTS 1, RECORD 2, PROBE_REQUEST 3, PROBE_REPLY 4. These
are descriptions, never permissions. Port 47900, 1200-byte control ceiling,
codecs and at-least-accepted ACK meaning stay unchanged.

Both payloads use shortest definite-length CBOR with exact tuple arity, no
trailing bytes and the existing inclusive 1,048,576-byte input bound before
allocation. The entire signed event, including the source wrapper, retains
the publication encoded-event bound. Unsupported schemas, vocabulary, identifiers/kinds,
duplicates, unsorted/empty lists, malformed identity/membership and malformed
CBOR refuse. Encoding also refuses invalid constructed values.

## Public pure API signatures

```rust
pub struct UsageProfilePublication {
    pub reporter: IdentityKey,
    pub profiles: Vec<UsageProfile>,
}
impl UsageProfilePublication {
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AccountError>;
    pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, AccountError>;
    pub fn validate_reporter(&self, expected: IdentityKey) -> Result<(), AccountError>;
}
pub struct NodeControlProfilePublication {
    pub membership_scope: MembershipScope,
    pub capabilities: Vec<u8>,
}
impl NodeControlProfilePublication {
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AccountError>;
    pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, AccountError>;
    pub fn validate_membership(&self, accepted: &MembershipScope) -> Result<(), AccountError>;
}
pub enum ProfilePublicationPayload {
    Usage(UsageProfilePublication),
    NodeControl(NodeControlProfilePublication),
}
impl PublicationEvent<'_> {
    pub fn decode_profile_payload(&self) -> Result<Option<ProfilePublicationPayload>, AccountError>;
}
```

The publication mapping recognizes only exact `(9, "usage-profile")` and
`(10, "node-control-profile")` pairs. It returns None for other kinds and empty
payloads, preserving the publication contract's explicit complete-empty withdrawal. No empty identity
or membership represents withdrawal. Publication decisions reject malformed
nonempty profile payloads before exposing replacement. Usage mapping also compares
the reporter with the signed recipient; callers must still supply the independent
expected reporter. Node-control consumers must compare the accepted membership
before committing the replacement. Neither payload authenticates itself. Existing
source binding, issuer/recipient, scope, channel, signature, completeness, expiry
and durable per-key version checks remain necessary.

Replacement or withdrawal clears only the corresponding exact scope's catalogue:
usage `units,reporters,parameters`, control `vocabulary,capabilities`. Historical
usage, pending reports, received control state and independently accepted control
authority remain consumer-owned. Missing or rejected input cannot reserve a
version, renew validity or replace state.

## Independent vectors and replacement sequence

The Python standard-library producer `tools/vectors/nsvec/producers/profile_publications.py`
implements these tuples independently of Rust. The consumer uses
`crates/nsshared-proto/tests/fixtures/vectors/profile-publications.vec`.
Every negative case records its exact input and refusal. Existing usage report/ACK
and Node-control fixtures retain their bytes; the family registry set is unchanged.

`profile_publication_replacement` consumes install-usage, install-control,
malformed-replacement, withdraw-usage, then replay-usage. The malformed version 2
must not reserve its version; the valid withdrawal at version 2 must succeed.
Only the exact usage key is withdrawn, while control remains installed. Retained
version tombstones refuse the older install after a consumer restart. Runtime
persistence and preservation of captured usage/control state belong to the gateway
regression, which must consume these same source-bound bytes. Shared tests exercise
pure decisions and externally retained versions only, with no runtime or I/O.

Fixture issuer is Ed25519 seed `02` repeated 32 times, recipient/reporter seed
`01` repeated 32 times, membership IDs are `03` repeated 16 times. Stream source
binding and delivery use the existing exact source-selection encodings. Signature
domains remain `ns.account.publication.v1\0`, `ns.account.source-binding.v1\0`
and `ns.account.source-publication.v1\0`, each with a final zero separator.
The fixture file records inner/outer canonical bytes and exact signatures. The
following canonical bytes and signatures are fixed before codec implementation.
